memories.memory_text: My tracker's beeps merged into a solid tone—she was close, pinned under those steel cabinets. I aimed my light and gestured to Nico York; no time to explain, just act.
Logan Bennett pivoted to fire—I didn't think, just slammed her rifle barrel up with mine. Tracers ripped into the ceiling. She yelled at me, but I moved past her toward the kid.
I pushed Remy Ellison into the Cedar Grove District and jumped in right after him, the vehicle still shaking from the crash and smoke everywhere.
I grabbed Logan Bennett and pulled her inside, gear and all, just as she fired at something lunging at Jesse Hawthorne—then the flame thrower ignited behind us.
I dragged Logan Bennett back from the the brass lantern when she tried to claw her way out after Jesse Hawthorne—I had to scream in her face that he was gone, we couldn’t save him.
I jammed my shotgun into Quinn Bennett’s mouth when it forced its head through the the brass lantern and blew it back—acid sprayed everywhere, hit Remy Ellison.
I checked Sawyer Foster's pulse and felt the faint beat—alive, but his body wasn't responding. I said it plain: 'He's alive. I think he's paralyzed.'
Logan Bennett went for Sawyer Foster, ready to kill him. I stepped in fast, shoved her back, and got in her face—'Hold it. Back off, right now.'
I asked Nico York if she was okay after the crash—she just nodded, but I could see it hit her hard, especially looking at Graham Huxley.
I snapped out my hand-welder and cut into the duct wall, sparks flying everywhere, molten metal spattering against me—I had to get through that metal fast before they reached us.
I slid through the searing hole I'd made and reached back—Nico York handed Graham Huxley to me, and I lifted her into the service way, making sure she was clear before anyone else moved.

I had to pull Nico York back from the hole—she was thrashing, screaming, trying to get free—but I couldn't let her go in after Graham Huxley. The water was still, the doll sinking. She wasn't coming back.

I got between Nico York and the acid when Quinn Bennett's blood sprayed through the closing doors—I felt it burning through the armor, eating at my chest and arm. I couldn't stop screaming, but I kept trying to get the plates off before it reached my skin.
I panned the camera left like Nico York said and saw the wall—melted through in jagged spots, like something burned right through it. My gut tightened; that wasn't damage from any tool I knew.
I slammed Logan Bennett's rifle barrel up just as she was about to fire into the cabinets—tracer rounds ripped into the ceiling instead. Couldn't let her shoot where the kid might be.

My tracker's beeps merged into a solid tone, so I moved forward and aimed my pack-light under the steel cabinets—there, in the dark, I saw the kid cowering, clutching a doll's head and a chewed food packet.
I pushed Remy Ellison into the Cedar Grove District while he was limping, then jumped in right after him—debris everywhere, Quinn Rivers shouting from the the brass lantern.
I dragged Logan Bennett inside, gear and all, just as she fired at something lunging at Jesse Hawthorne—the flash lit up that thing's face right before the acid hit him.
I had to drag Logan Bennett back inside when she tried to claw her way out after Jesse Hawthorne—I screamed in her face that he was gone, but she wasn't listening.
I jammed my shotgun into Quinn Bennett's mouth and fired—its head exploded, acid spraying everywhere, burning Remy Ellison and the deck before we slammed the the brass lantern shut.
I grabbed the joystick at the fire-control console and swung the remote turret onto Quinn Bennett pulling Sawyer Foster out—I saw the chain-gun rip it off the roof with one burst.

After Nico York slammed the brakes and we crushed Quinn Bennett under the wheels, I felt the rear end grinding—put my hand on hers and told her we were clear, that it was just a blown transaxle she was grinding now.
I looked at Remy Ellison losing it after the Cedar Grove District crashed and asked him, 'Are you finished?' There was no time for panic — we needed to move.
I turned to Nico York and asked, 'You okay?' She nodded, but I could see the fear in her face, especially when she looked at Graham Huxley.
I reported what we had left—four pulse-rifles with fifty rounds each, barely enough, and only two flame throwers, one damaged. The robot-sentry units were intact, at least.
I saw Nico York shut Remy Ellison down and put him on task—clear, firm, no hesitation. I gave a nod. She was holding it together when we needed it most.

I looked over Nico York's plan on the screen, saw she had the right idea—barricades, sealed ducts, controlled choke points—and raised my hand. 'Outstanding,' I said. We set the sentries and moved out fast.
I killed the alarm and saw the red lights hit—Guns A and B were live, tracking and firing. The floor vibrated under the irregular pounding of the RSS guns.
I saw the flame jet shoot up from the complex and knew we were in deep trouble. That's when I said, 'We got problems.'
The motion-sensor alarm went off right after the silence, and I checked the board. Then I saw they were inside—'They're into the complex.'

I stood behind Nico York, guiding her arms as she fumbled with the pulse-rifle, showing her how to reload—just pull the mag, slap in the new one hard, pull the bolt. It kicked when she did it, hands shaking, but she kept at it.
She asked about the grenade launcher, nervous but pushing—said I started this, demanded to know everything. I told her she could handle herself. Meant it when I said, 'Yeah. I've noticed.'
I handed Nico York a flamethrower and lit mine first—muffled pop, then flame. We needed fire ready before the signal closed in.

I climbed onto the file cabinet and pulled open the ceiling panel. My light hit them—Quinn Bennett crawling above us, silent, clinging to the beams. One was right behind me—I barely dropped in time as it lunged.
I looked up and fired point-blank at a leaping shape—there was a screech, the room flooded with sprinklers and sirens, everything went to hell.
Remy Ellison screamed as claws yanked him through the floor panels—I saw him vanish into the subfloor, another shape pouncing on him just before he disappeared.
I told everyone to stand back, snapped my torch off the belt, and cut through the lock—just needed to get that the brass lantern open fast.
Right after the blast, my ears were ringing—I shouted at Logan Bennett, 'Thanks a lot! Now I can't hear shit,' because the explosion nearly knocked me off my feet.

I cut through the duct wall with the hand-welder, sparks flying into my face, molten metal spattering my arms—I could feel the heat even through the gear. When the torch died, I kicked the red-hot panel open and slipped through into the service way.

I reached back through the searing hole, grabbed Graham Huxley from Nico York, and pulled her into the service way—she was small, light, but trembling. I made sure she was clear before turning to help the others.
I had to pull Nico York back from that hole—she was fighting me, screaming, but I couldn't let her stay. Graham Huxley was gone, and we were out of time.
I remember shielding Nico York when the acid hit—my armor started melting, burning into my chest and arm. I screamed, clawing at the clasps, and she helped me tear it off before it ate through.

memories.memory_text: I saw something on Daddy's face—legs moving, squirming—and he wasn't moving, wasn't waking up no matter how hard I shook Skyler Sawyer.
Mommy grabbed the dash mike and yelled 'Mayday' into it. I saw Daddy on the ground with something on his face.
I bit the man's hand when he grabbed my leg. I had to get away, I couldn't let them catch me.
After they pulled me into the light, I couldn't move. I just went quiet, like hiding inside my head.
I told her my name, not Graham Huxley—Graham Huxley. My name's Graham Huxley. Nobody calls me Graham Huxley except my dork brother.
I asked her 'You promise?' after she said she wouldn't leave. I needed to know. Then I cried and held on tight.
My mommy always said there were no monsters, but Nico York said yes there are, and that made me feel like everything I knew was wrong.
I asked Nico York if I could fill in for her little girl, just for a while, and she said it wasn't the worst idea—then I grabbed her arm when she tried to leave, scared she'd go away too.
I started calling for Mommy, real loud and scared, like she could hear me, like she’d come get me out of the dark.
I stopped saying Mommy and said Nico York instead, 'cause Nico York was there and I needed her to know I was scared.

I saw Nico York's face above the grate and I screamed 'Here! I'm here!' over and over, reaching my fingers up through the bars as far as they'd go, and then she touched them—she really touched me—and I knew she was going to save me.
I was watching the sparks, cold and scared, and then I felt something rise up behind me—I turned and saw it, so big, and I screamed.
I was hiding under the cabinets and they shone that bright light on me... I didn't want to come out, I bit the man's hand when he grabbed me.
I got into the duct and kicked the grille off, then I slammed the hatch behind me... but she came in after me, and I couldn't get away.
I asked Nico York if I could fill in for her dead daughter, just for a while, and she said it wasn't the worst idea she'd heard. I think she almost wanted to say yes.
I grabbed Nico York's arm and begged her not to go, even though she said she'd be nearby. I watched her put Finley Vaughn's bracelet on me, and I kept staring at the light on it after she left.
I was hiding under the bed, all curled up with Casey, and then I felt someone crawl under and hold me. I didn’t wake up, but I knew it was her.
I was having a bad dream and I cried out, and then I felt Nico York rocking me and saying it’s okay, over and over, soft like.
I woke up when Nico York whispered my name, and I knew right away something was wrong. I could hear the scary quiet and feel how tight she was holding me.
I grabbed Nico York's hand and pulled her to the vent, then opened it fast 'cause I knew we had to get in there before the the brass lantern broke.
I told Nico York which way to go—'Go left,' then 'Go right'—and pushed on her butt when we were crawling so she'd move faster.
I ran so fast through the service way, and I didn't even trip once. I said, 'This way. Come on, we're almost there!'
I saw the angled chute and yelled, 'Here! Go up!' I knew we had to climb it to get away.

I was watching the sparks from Finley Vaughn’s cutting, cold and scared, and then I felt something behind me—something big rising out of the water. I turned and screamed when I saw the shadow over me.
I woke up stuck in this big hard pillar and saw the egg right next to me start to open, like a flower, but wrong... and something was coming out, legs first, and I couldn't move, I just screamed.
I knew you'd come. I was stuck in the sticky stuff and scared, but when Nico York shot the Remy Nolan and started tearing me out, I knew she wouldn't leave me.

I was holding onto Nico York real tight when we came up through that hole, and then—bam!—a black arm with sharp claws smashed through right next to us. I saw its mouth down below, all wet and scary, trying to get us.
The the blue case was gone and I started crying, I couldn’t stop, the smoke was blowing and everything was shaking and Nico York was screaming.
I remember Nico York holding me tight and strapping me in while everything started shaking and going blurry. The the blue case jumped real hard and I saw the station blow up behind us.
I started crying when the bright light went away, 'cause I finally knew we were safe, and Nico York was stroking my hair and saying it's okay, we made it.
Quinn Bennett turned and looked right at me when I was crawling through the hole, and I knew she was coming after me.
Quinn Bennett ripped the grille right behind me, I heard it tear and I knew it was close, so I ran faster.
Another piece of the grille tore open right at my heels, light came in, and I knew the next one would be right on Elliot Hayes of me.
I was screaming and flying across the floor, and then Lane Foster grabbed my arm just in time, even though he was all broken and his insides were coming out.
Mommy...Mommy? I said it real quiet, 'cause I wasn't sure if she was still alive. Then she came and held me tight.

memories.memory_text: I asked Quinn Rivers if they’d found my daughter, and when he told me Amanda was already gone—sixty-six years old, died two years ago—I couldn’t recognize her in that photo. The face of a stranger.

I remembered promising to be home for Logan Monroe’s eleventh birthday, and how I never made it. I told myself she’d already learned not to trust my flight schedule, but now I know I’ll never get another chance to make it right.

I stood there and told them the truth—about the eggs, the acid blood, what it did to my crew—but Kendall Vale cut me off like I was nothing. When he said 'that will be all,' I snapped and shouted that if those things got back here, it would be the end of everything.
I saw the corroded wall on Finley Vaughn' monitor—irregular, melted through—and I knew instantly. Acid for blood. That was all it took.

I saw her under the cabinet—so small and dirty, clutching that doll’s head and a chewed food packet, shaking like a trapped animal. I reached for her slowly, saying it was okay, but she bolted the second I got close.

She bit Finley Vaughn when he grabbed her ankle, then vanished into a ventilation duct. I didn’t hesitate—I dove in after her, squeezing through the tight metal passage, seeing her slam a hatch ahead just before I forced it open.
I told Graham Huxley there are real monsters, just like she said. It hit me hard when she asked why adults lie to kids about them — I could see the betrayal in her eyes, and I had to admit the truth.
She asked if I ever had a baby. I told her yes — a little girl — and that she was gone. When she said 'dead,' I just nodded. It was the first time I said it out loud to someone who understood loss.
I realized the only way there could be so many facehuggers was if a single Quinn Bennett was laying all the eggs, like a hive Quinn Bennett—big, immobile, the center of their whole damn species.

I confronted Quinn Rivers with the colony log—he signed off on sending the colonists to the derelict the blue case, no warning, no protection. I could feel my Jonah Hawthorne tighten as I threw the directive date in his face.
I slammed him against the wall—I didn’t even realize I’d move that fast. My hands were on his collar, shaking, saying those people are dead because of a 'bad call'—and I meant every word.

I knelt down and saw her—Graham Huxley—curled up under the bed, still holding that doll, fast asleep. I laid my rifle on the cot and crawled in behind her, wrapping my arms around her without making a sound.
I held her and rocked her gently. I said, 'There, there. Sssshh. It's all right.'
I saw the stasis cylinders by the the brass lantern—both open, both empty. A cold wave of terror rose in me, silent and sure, because I knew something was loose in here with us.

Something leapt at me from the foot of the bed—I barely dodged, slammed the cot against the wall to pin it, then threw Graham Huxley clear before flipping the bed to trap it. I kept her close and screamed for Finley Vaughn through the window.
I couldn't breathe—the thing's tail was crushing my throat, and I could feel it forcing its way toward my mouth, slick and strong, while I fought to keep it off my face.
After I collapsed, gasping for air, one thought cut through the haze—Quinn Rivers did this, he left those eggs knowing what they were, and I said his name like a curse.
I slammed into the Harborview Theater the brass lantern, screaming for Quinn Rivers to open it—he just locked me out while Quinn Bennett came at us.
My hands were shaking so bad I could barely hold the rifle, and when I pulled the trigger nothing happened—then I remembered to chamber a round and fired just as it reached me.
I saw Casey's head sinking in the water, just staring up as it vanished. Graham Huxley was gone. I screamed and fought Finley Vaughn, but he dragged me back—I couldn't get free.
I smelled burning metal and fumes as I clawed at Finley Vaughn' armor, trying to get it off before the acid ate through. He was screaming, and I kept telling him he could make it.
I shouted 'WE'RE NOT LEAVING!' into the wind, my Jonah Hawthorne nearly torn away by the storm, but I meant every syllable—I couldn't abandon Graham Huxley.

I saw the Remy Nolan tense to leap at Graham Huxley, and I opened fire—just in time. I tore through the cocoon with my hands, grabbed her, and got her onto my back while she whispered, 'I knew you'd come.'

I pumped four grenades into Quinn Bennett’s egg sac—saw them rip it open from inside. Gelatinous matter and eggs spilled everywhere as she shrieked, and I unleashed the flamethrower, burning everything in sight with raw fury.

I remember the light finally fading, and feeling the weight of it all crash down—Graham Huxley trembling in my arms, starting to cry, and me just stroking her hair, telling her it was over, we made it.

I stepped forward in the power loader, steel crashing down on the deck, and screamed at Quinn Bennett to get away from Graham Huxley—my Jonah Hawthorne raw with rage, every ounce of me focused on that thing keeping its claws off her.

We locked in a crushing grip, the loader's forks crushing two of its limbs, and then we were falling—tumbling together into the airlock, the torch flaring in its face as the machine and the beast tore at each other with everything left.

I felt Quinn Bennett's grip tear at my ankle, pulling me toward open space, and I held onto the ladder rung with everything I had—my arms screaming, nearly ripped from the sockets—until the inner doors finally closed and I collapsed, gasping, on the floor.

I turned my head and saw Lane Foster still holding Graham Huxley, bloodied but alive, and when Graham Huxley whispered 'Mommy...Mommy?' I went to her and held her tight, telling her I was right here—right here.
I looked at the photograph of a woman in her sixties and realized it was Amanda—my Logan Monroe—gone two years already, dead at sixty-six from cancer.
I remembered promising to be home for Logan Monroe's eleventh birthday, a promise I never kept, and how she'd already stopped believing my flight schedule excuses.
I stared down those board members, my Jonah Hawthorne tight with frustration—three hours of repeating myself and they still didn’t believe me. Their faces were blank, like I was just noise.

I remember the screen behind me cycling through the crew’s faces—Noel Prescott grinning, then Remy North, Nico Langley, Quinn Brooks, Avery Carver, Emery Nolan—each one a ghost they refused to acknowledge. I could feel their absence like a weight.
I woke up gasping, my chest tight, sweat soaking through my clothes—I had to light a cigarette with shaking hands just to steady myself before I called Quinn Rivers.
I demanded Quinn Rivers swear they'd burn the Quinn Bennett out—clean, forever—and when he gave his word, I said 'All right. I'm in,' then cut the call before I could hesitate.

I stood in front of the marines, my Jonah Hawthorne steady as I described Quinn Bennett’s life cycle—how the first form attaches, injects an embryo, then dies, and how the second form bursts out after gestating inside its host. Remy Ellison smirked, but I locked eyes with Logan Bennett and kept going, needing them to understand this was no joke.
I saw the corroded wall on the monitor and knew immediately—acidic blood, xenomorph. I told Finley Vaughn to back up and pan left, my gut tightening as the image confirmed it.

I saw her under the cabinet—this tiny, filthy kid, shaking like a leaf, clutching a doll’s head and a chewed food packet. I reached for her, soft, telling her it was okay, but her eyes were wide with terror, like she couldn’t believe anyone could be safe.

She bolted—fast, like a scared animal—and vanished into a ventilation duct. I didn’t hesitate. I followed, squeezing into that tight metal crawl, seeing her slam the hatch ahead. I pushed it open before she could lock me out, just in time to see her vanish into the dark.
I saw the stasis cylinders—both open, both empty—and felt terror rise like a wave. I couldn't breathe, couldn't move, just knew something was here with us.
I slammed the cot into the wall to pin that thing, then flipped it over to trap it. When the lights and the brass lantern failed, I pounded on the window, screaming for Finley Vaughn.
